The origin of red luminescence in o-phenylenediamine-based carbon dots
abstract: Carbon dots (CDs) prepared from o -phenylenediamine (oPD) have attracted significant research interest, because they can exhibit blue, green, or red fluorescence depending on synthetic conditions and dopants. The red- and NIR-emitting oPD-based CDs are of particular interest because of their potential for bioimaging and biomedical applications. Efforts to understand the relationship between their structure and optical properties have led to the proposal of various hypotheses of the red luminescence, which are however difficult to support due to limited knowledge of their precise structural…

title: Fluorine-Enabled Photochemical Generation of Carbonyl Ylide 1,3-Dipoles
abstract: The photochemistry of carbonyl compounds underpins a wide range of modern synthetic transformations. However, photoinduced rearrangements, despite their unique potential for skeletal reorganization, remain conspicuously underexplored. Here, we show that fluorine can be used as a design principle to divert these reactions from established photochemical pathways. Mechanistic investigations combining experimental, spectroscopic and computational approaches support an unusual singlet excited state pathway involving initial cyclization followed by skeletal rearrangement.

title: New-to-Nature Transformation for the Z-Selective Synthesis of Unsaturated Acids via Acyl Azolium Intermediates
abstract: Organocatalytic methods operating via α,β-unsaturated acyl azolium intermediates are extensively studied in organic chemistry and typically proceed through E-configured intermediates that dictate the stereochemical outcome of the final product. To date, the use of this species within enzymatic systems is restricted to a single natural biosynthetic pathway. Herein, we report an example of a versatile new-to-nature biocatalytic transformation that harnesses an α,β-unsaturated acyl azolium intermediate within the active site of a thiaminedependent enzyme.

title: Understanding Composition-Dependent Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability of (101)-Oriented RuxTi1-xO2
abstract: Rutile RuO 2 is a highly active catalyst for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) but hindered by its high rates of dissolution under reaction conditions. Substitution with elements forming more stable oxides, such as Ti, is an appealing strategy to increase stability. In such solid solutions, the intrinsic activity (and stability) of a given active site is expected to depend on its local environment and the identity of neighboring metal centers.

title: Harnessing Thiol-Tetrazine Bond Exchange for Engineering Dynamic Covalent Hydrogels for Cell Culture
abstract: Dynamic covalent chemistry (DCvC) provides a versatile toolbox of reactions forming reversible covalent bonds that are strong yet dynamic. Implementing DCvC in hydrogel networks to engineer extracellular matrix (ECM) mimics improves their resemblance to natural tissues, by conferring dynamicity and time-dependent viscoelastic properties. In this work, the nucleophilic aromatic substitution of tetrazines with thiols (thiol-Tz) is proposed as a DCvC strategy to synthesize tunable, dynamic hydrogels under close-to-physiological conditions, which find value as scaffolds for cell encapsulation.

title: What an SO(3) orientation flow can and cannot learn in molecular-crystal structure prediction
abstract: Rigid-body factorization is an appealing route to molecular-crystal structure prediction: freezing each molecule’s conformer reduces a crystal to a lattice, a set of fractional centroids on the torus T3, and a per-molecule orientation on SO(3). Whether the orientation field is actually learnable on real molecular crystals has not been examined. We introduce SymMC-Flow, a space-groupconditioned rigid-body flow on lattice×T3×SO(3), used as a diagnostic study on 1,127 crystals from the Cambridge Structural Database.

title: Coupled-perturbed extended tight-binding for analytic Hessians, infrared and Raman spectra
abstract: We present an analytic response formalism for harmonic vibrational spectroscopy with the extended tight-binding (xTB) family of electronic-structure methods. A fieldspace coupled-perturbed self-consistent-charge treatment delivers molecular polarizabilities and, via the interchange theorem, analytic dipole derivatives (atomic polar tensors). Carrying the same formalism to nuclear perturbations yields closed-form analytic nuclear Hessians, which combine a metric-perturbed coupled-perturbed solve with explicit second-derivative terms built on dedicated integral kernels, and whose response…

title: Extraction Strategies for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS): A Critical Comparative Framework Integrating Sensitivity, Sustainability, and Analytical Trade-offs
abstract: Sample preparation, not instrumental detection, limits PFAS (per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances) quantification to current regulatory thresholds. This review covers 35 PFAS-specific extraction methods, including dispersive solid-phase extraction and solid-phase microextraction (dSPE/SPME, n = 15), liquid-phase microextraction (LPME, n = 7), and magnetic particle-based extraction (MSPE/DSPE, n = 13).

title: Reversible Site-Selective Editing of Atomically Precise Au6 Nanoclusters through Controlled Oxidative Addition/Reductive Elimination
abstract: Enacting precise bond formations and dissociations at specific sites is focal to molecular editing of functional materials but remains difficult to achieve on the surfaces of metal nanoparticles. Here, we demonstrate the first site-selective molecular editing of a multidentate ligand-stabilized [Au6(SbP3)2][PF6]2 (Au6) nanocluster (where, SbP3= tris(2-(diphenylphosphino)phenyl)stibine), using iodobenzene dichloride (PhICl2).

title: Machine Learning for High-Throughput Reaction Yield Prediction in DNA-Encoded Library Synthesis
abstract: DNA-encoded library (DEL) synthesis relies on efficient DNA-compatible reactions to ensure library fidelity and the reliability of downstream affinity selection. However, most existing reaction yield prediction models were developed for general organic synthesis and typically use full-atom representations of complete reactants and products. In DEL single-cycle synthesis validation, an appropriate model reaction is to focus on the exposed reactive handle, its local chemical environment, the incoming building block (BB), and the reaction type, rather than large constant backgrounds such as the…

title: Chain Cluster Diffusion and Network Relaxation in Poly(vinyl alcohol) and Borax Solutions
abstract: The physical chemistry of poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) and borax solutions reflects the formation of dynamic covalent borate anion cross-links between chains. Due to the reversible linkages, PVA and borax solutions not only exhibit re-entrant phase behavior, but they also display distinct fast and slow relaxations. While the fast regime corresponds to single chain and small cluster diffusion, the slow regime transitions from large cluster diffusion to reversible network relaxation as the borax concentration increases.

title: Stereoselective Dearomative [2π+2σ] Cycloadditions of Indoles Enabled by Triplet-State Iminium Ion Reactivity
abstract: We report an organocatalytic enantioselective [2π+2σ] cycloaddition mediated by visible-light for the dearomatization of indoles. The transformation provides rapid access to complex and sp3-rich indoline-based polycycles with excellent levels of diastereo- and enantiocontrol (up to >20:1 d.r. and 96% ee), through the tripletstate reactivity of a chiral iminium ion.

title: Catalyst-Free, Visible-Light-Driven Hydrogenation and Giese Addition of N-Hydroxyphthalimide Ester–Containing Polymers Using Hantzsch Esters
abstract: To address unfavorable monomer reactivity ratios and catalyst deactivation during olefin copolymerization with polar vinyl monomers, alternative synthesis methods, such as the postfunctionalization of N-hydroxyphthalimide (NHPI) ester–containing polymers, have attracted significant attention. Although conventional hydrogenation methods have successfully yielded olefin copolymers, they are limited due to their reliance on toxic, unstable reagents and significant scale-up challenges.

title: TAME: Element-wise Mixture-of-Experts Fusion for Data-Efficient and Interpretable Molecular Property Prediction
abstract: Property prediction for molecules and materials is bottlenecked by label scarcity, and in this regime the operative failure mode is not a low mean but an unpredictable tail: individual training runs collapse. The three dominant molecular representations fail in complementary ways—physicochemical descriptors are exact but fixed, graph neural networks learn topology but degenerate under sparse supervision, and language models supply semantic context but cannot compute exact quantities—yet combining them is itself the learning problem, because modality-level scalar gating commits the whole model…

title: Ag13Cu4 Nanocluster-Catalyzed Ambient C-F Bond Activation
abstract: Atomically precise nanoclusters (NC) with discrete electronic states and high surface-to-atom ratios offer unique controllable active sites leading to unique catalytic transformations. Here we demonstrate that an ultrasmall (<3 nm), atomically precise Ag-Cu alloy NC, [Ag13Cu4(o1-CBT)12]3- (o1-CBT = ortho-1-carboranethiol) (Ag13Cu4), leverages these features to accomplish the extremely difficult activation and cleavage of inert C-F bond under ambient conditions.

title: Transport Cross Sections and Collisional Energy Relaxation of Superthermal O(3P) Atoms in N2 for Planetary Aeronomy
abstract: Superthermal (“hot”) oxygen atoms deposit their energy in planetary upper atmospheres and in hypersonic shock layers through collisions with N2, but the rate at which they do so is set not by the magnitude of the collision cross section, which is dominated by forward diffraction, but by transport-weighted moments of the differential cross section (DCS). We derive momentum-transfer and viscosity cross sections, mean collisional deflections, and energy-relaxation rates for O(3P) + N2 from our previously reported quantum coupled-channel DCSs, for 16O, 17O, and 18O over collision energies…

title: Systematic evaluation of LLM-based zero-shot model construction in chemistry and materials science: predictive performance and response reliability
abstract: Purely data-driven materials exploration is often constrained by limited experimental data, motivating exploration strategies that leverage prior knowledge of the target material system encoded in large language models (LLMs). This paper describes an approach that combines LLM-derived pairwise comparisons with preference learning to construct utility-function models that rank experimental conditions with respect to a target property, without directly using measured target-property values for the system of interest either during LLM inference or model fitting.

title: GeoDSSOP: Geometry-aware prediction of protein backbone order parameters from sequence and structure
abstract: Backbone amide order parameters (S2) describe protein motions on the picosecond-to-nanosecond time scale at residue resolution. However, NMR measurement and calculation from atomistic molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories are time-consuming. We developed GeoDSSOP (Geometry-aware Deep Sequence–Structure Order-Parameter Predictor) to predict backbone N–H S2 from one amino-acid sequence and one corresponding structure. GeoDSSOP combines frozen ESM-2 residue embeddings with a geometric vector perceptron-style encoder of a residue graph.

title: Ethanol-Oriented CO2 Hydrogenation for Alcoholto-Jet Sustainable Aviation Fuels: Catalyst Design and Fixed-Bed Performance Benchmarking
abstract: Sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) is expected to play a central role in aviation decarbonization because long-range flights will continue to depend on energy-dense, infrastructure-compatible liquid fuels. Among available SAF pathways, alcohol-to-jet (ATJ) routes connect oxygenated intermediates with established upgrading technologies for jet-range hydrocarbons. In this context, alcohol-oriented thermocatalytic CO 2 hydrogenation could provide an upstream platform for SAF production when coupled with low-carbon H 2 .

title: Electronic configuration vectors provide transferable elemental representations for machine learning across the periodic table
abstract: Machine learning models typically represent elements as discrete identities, limiting inference for elements absent from training. We introduce the electronic configuration vector (ECV), a physically grounded representation derived from the Aufbau principle that continuously encodes orbital occupancies and energetics across elements. Principal component analysis reveals low-dimensional manifolds that organize elements by atomic number, with extrema corresponding to block transitions.

title: Fast Fourier Transform-Based Approach to Denoise and Enhance GC×GC-TOFMS Data
abstract: Comprehensive two-dimensional (2D) gas chromatography mass spectrometry (GC×GC-MS) provides improved separation quality in comparison to one-dimensional (1D) GC-MS; however, it presents with undesirable noise akin to that of 1D, including background chemical, thermal, and electrical noise. In GC×GC-MS, the narrow peak widths necessitate the use of a fast detector, often a time-of-flight mass spectrometer (TOFMS), acquiring more than 50 spectra per second (Hz). These high detector speeds increase electrical noise.

title: Finite-temperature dynamic stability separates foundation machine-learning interatomic potentials that harmonic benchmarks rank equally
abstract: Foundation (universal) machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are now used routinely as cheap stand-ins for DFT in high-throughput stability screening, but they are benchmarked almost exclusively against harmonic (0 K) phonons. Dynamic stability is physically a finite-temperature property, and an important class of materials, including cubic perovskites, bcc refractory metals and cubic fluorites, is harmonically unstable but thermally stabilised by anharmonicity.

title: Force-Dependent Fracture of Dynamic Polymer Networks: Sacrificial Bond Rupture and Dispersion-Induced Physical Crosslinking
abstract: We use coarse-grained molecular dynamics to investigate tensile fracture in dynamically crosslinked polymer networks, where both weak-linker and strong backbone bonds rupture according to Bell-model force-dependent probabilities. Competition between these pathways determines whether preferential weak-linker rupture relieves local stress, redistributes load, and protects the backbone. Lower linker activation energy or stretching stiffness promotes this sacrificial pathway, suppressing backbone rupture and delaying failure.

title: An unlearnable target: diagnosing the orientation gauge in PXRD-conditioned molecular-crystal flow matching
abstract: Rigid-body flow matching reduces a molecular crystal to a lattice, fractional cen-troids and per-molecule orientations on SO(3), and is an attractive route to structure determination from powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD). We report a negative result and its root cause. Our PXRD-conditioned rigid-body flow recovered 0 of 160 held-out structures, and the failure was neither the lattice nor the sampler: a frame-preserving oracle substitution shows that installing the ground-truth unit cell into the generated packing yields 0/10 matches, while a component decomposition on held-out data puts the…

title: Irradiation wavelength tuned stepwise [2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives as a platform for light-mechanical energy conversion
abstract: Cyclobutane motifs are widely embedded in natural products, and [2+2] cycloaddition is a facile method to synthesize four-membered rings. In general, controlling the regioselectivity and stereoselectivity of cycloaddition remains a great challenge. Nevertheless, the prearrangement of the reactant molecules in topo-photochemical reaction can place the atoms in the products at specific positions. In this work, the irradiation wavelength-controlled, stepwise photo-induced [2+2] cycloaddition of indolylphenylpropenone derivatives took place in crystals.

title: A Human Audit of AI-Generated Theoretical Chemistry: Lessons from Ten Chapter-Level Peer Reviews
abstract: AI-assisted study spanning molecular stability, the Born–Oppenheimer approximation, chemical bonding, density functional theory, electron correlation, reaction dynamics, thermodynamics, kinetics, and transport. Across the available referee reports, all ten chapters were recommended for acceptance after minor revision within the assessment rubric used in the review project, and no confirmed substantive error was identified that invalidated a principal scientific conclusion. The main value of the project does not lie in claiming ten new fundamental theorems.

title: PXRD-Diff: diagnosing the encoder bottleneck in diffusion-based powder-diffraction structure inversion, with classical autoindexing as a drop-in remedy
abstract: Inverting a one-dimensional powder X-ray diffraction (PXRD) pattern to a three-dimensional crystal structure remains an open problem, and recent generative approaches report results under mutually incompatible protocols with failure modes seldom catalogued. PXRD-Diff, a 3.7 M-parameter conditional diffusion model trained on the CDVAE MP-20 split, is presented, and DiffractGPT, PXRDnet and deCIFer are reproduced through the same pymatgen StructureMatcher harness.

title: Observation Deviation as a Quantitative Observability Measure of Weak Chemical Features in Analytical Measurements
abstract: When a chemical signal recedes into noise, deciding whether a weak chemical feature is still worth observing - and where observation should stop - is usually delegated to signal-to-noise conventions, software parameters, or an analyst’s personal judgment. We propose Observation Deviation (τ), a dimensionless measure of chemical-feature observability, that turns this tacit judgment into a quantifiable analytical variable. Within a stated observation protocol, τ quantifies how much an analytical chemical feature deviates from the local profile its observation anticipates.

title: Reactivity Over Recognition: Covalent Screening of Natural Products against Falcipain-2 and Falcipain-3
abstract: We present a reproducible, reactivity-weighted covalent-screening workflow that separates molecular recognition, intrinsic electrophile reactivity, and matched host-protease covalent capture, and we validate it before applying it. Screening 1,012 South African Natural Compounds Database entries against falcipain-2 and falcipain-3, a warhead/β-accessibility cascade retained 185 compounds, and a consensus of recognition docking, uniform-mode covalent docking, MM-GBSA, DFT reactivity descriptors, and predicted developability prioritized SANC00867.

title: Current landscape and research gaps in artificial intelligence for ophthalmic nursing: a scoping review
abstract: IntroductionArtificial intelligence (AI) is advancing rapidly across clinical medicine, yet its application within ophthalmic nursing, spanning emergency triage, perioperative care, day surgery, and patient education, remains poorly characterized. The growing burden of eye disease and the demand for community-based ophthalmic screening create an urgent context for understanding where AI can augment nursing capacity in this field and what barriers may be limiting evidence generation. This review aimed to systematically map published evidence on AI applications in ophthalmic nursing practice and education, characterize the technologies deployed and outcomes reported, and identify recurring research gaps and barriers through interpretive synthesis of the mapped literature.MethodsFour electronic databases (Web of Science Core Collections, PubMed, Scopus, and CINAHL) were searched from inception to June 12, 2026. Peer-reviewed English-language articles simultaneously addressing AI or machine learning, ophthalmology or eye conditions, and nurse engagement were eligible. Records were independently screened by two reviewers and data were extracted using a standardized charting form.ResultsFrom 254 records retrieved, 7 studies met the inclusion criteria (2023-2026). Applications spanned emergency triage and primary diagnosis, surgical nursing assistance (including one pre-clinical prototype without direct nurse involvement), day ward workflow management, and nursing education. Reported evaluation domains included triage or diagnostic performance, engineering detection performance, usability and acceptability, workflow efficiency, and educational outcomes. AI paradigms included classical machine learning, deep learning (convolutional neural networks), and large language models, deployed via clinical workflow interfaces, augmented reality, and robotic systems, and processing structured and multimodal data (image, text, audio).DiscussionDespite ophthalmology's prominent role in the early development of clinical AI, dedicated research on AI in ophthalmic nursing remains uncommon in the published literature. To our knowledge, this is the first scoping review to draw on international, English-language sources on this topic. Future research should prioritize nurse-led studies in community and primary care settings, broader modality exploration matched to nursing tasks, rigorous prospective evaluation of nursing-specific outcomes, and, where no current study exists, nurses as active co-designers of AI tools.

De novo generation and computational screening of dual-targeting short peptide inhibitors against PBP2b and PBP2x in drug-resistant Streptococcus Pneumoniae
abstract: Deep learning has greatly advanced de novo protein design, yet its application to rational short peptide design remains underexplored. Here, we developed SPB-Seeker (Short Peptide Binder Seeker), an integrated pipeline combining deep learning-based generative models with computational chemistry screening to discover dual-target short peptide inhibitors. Using penicillin-binding proteins PBP2b and PBP2x from drug-resistant Streptococcus pneumoniae as targets, AFDesign, RFdiffusion, and BoltzGen were employed to generate an initial library of 1101 candidate sequences.

title: Electrolyte Effects on N-Heterocyclic Imines as the Redox Sorbent for Electrochemical CO2 Capture
abstract: N-Heterocyclic imines (NHIs) represent a promising class of sorbents for electrochemically mediated carbon capture (EMCC) due to their ability to bind CO2 in the neutral state and operate reversibly at redox potentials more positive than that of oxygen. In this study, the effect of electrolyte composition on the thermochemical and electrochemical behavior of NHI-based systems is examined. Using reaction calorimetry and Raman and NMR spectroscopy, we demonstrate that Lewis acid cations stabilize the NHI–CO2 adduct through charged interactions, and the solvent and anion donor number tune this stabilization by modulating the effective cation Lewis acidity. As a result, electrolyte salts can substantially increase the magnitude of the NHI–CO2 reaction enthalpy, leading to higher CO2 loading on NHI at low CO2 partial pressure (10–3 atm) and faster capture kinetics. The impacts of the electrolyte selection on NHI redox behavior as well as oxygen reduction were also investigated. The findings indicate that electrolyte design must balance the strength of cation–NHI–CO2 stabilization, NHI redox activity, and the redox potential separation from oxygen reduction. By providing a mechanistic framework for how individual electrolyte components govern important process parameters, this work offers insights for optimizing electrolyte environments to achieve high-efficiency and reversible EMCC.

title: Quantum Light Spectroscopy
abstract: Spectroscopy based on individual-photon-level light sources brings new variables to both spectroscopy and imaging. We refer to this approach as quantum-light spectroscopy (QLS). The photon statistics of different types of photon sources and photon entanglements are briefly described. We then illustrate the potential of QLS by means of some current experimental examples including time-resolved spectroscopy performed with single photons and quantum-enhanced optical imaging, showing how all the methods rely on correlations between entangled photons in the pair. We then ask: how might physical chemists exploit QLSs to expose new physical insights? For example, can we address fundamental questions in interactions between light and molecules or materials that are very difficult to address with classical light sources? Does QLS open up techniques to study highly congested spectra with higher combined spectral and temporal resolution than is possible with classical light? The concept of QLS also opens the potential study of fundamental questions such as what initial excited states are produced by individual photon absorption? We also point out the experimental challenges in extending QLS to more complex spectroscopies, such as multidimensional spectroscopies. We conclude with a brief selection of recent theoretical proposals to extend the capabilities of the QLS.

title: Rational Engineering of the Radical SAM Enzyme HtkB Expands the Chemical Space of Cyclophane RiPPs
abstract: Cyclophane-containing peptides represent a structurally diverse class of macrocycles with important applications in drug development due to their stability and target specificity. Radical S-adenosylmethionine (rSAM) enzymes are key catalysts for cyclophane formation and execute chemically challenging C(sp2)–C(sp3) crosslinks. However, rSAM cyclophane synthases have generally been restricted to acting on their native or engineered substrates. Here, we report structure-guided engineering of an rSAM cyclophane synthase through mutation of a conserved D214 residue in the rSAM enzyme HtkB.

title: Neutrophil-Inspired Programmable Bacteria for Pyroptosis-Driven Tumor Eradication

title: Artificial Intelligence in Medicine: From Machine Learning to Generative and Multimodal Models — A Structured Narrative Review of Clinical Applications, Evidence Maturity, Challenges, and Future Directions
abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence (AI) has evolved from rule-based expert systems to statistical machine learning, deep learning, foundation models, generative artificial intelligence, and large multimodal models. This technological progression has expanded the potential role of AI in medicine from narrowly defined diagnostic tasks to medical imaging, clinical decision support, electronic health record analysis, documentation, patient communication, biomedical research, drug discovery, and medical education.
